MAP ANSWER REVIEW CARD
Ahmadreza Samadi | Start with the decision.

A copyable note for reviewing a question about a map. Adapted from:
https://a-samadi.com/writing/geospatial-ai-map-answer-review.html

This is a proposed editorial workflow, not a validated assessment or a test
of a particular AI product. Completing it does not establish that a source
is accurate, suitable for the decision, or sufficient to assess a property.

BLANK CARD — COPY THIS SECTION

Question and intended use:
[What do you want to know, and what would you use the answer to decide?]

AREA
Question concerns: [point, building, parcel, neighbourhood or wider area]
Evidence describes: [the area actually represented by the source]
Match or unresolved difference: [explain; do not assume a match]

PERIOD
Relevant observation date or interval: [value and what it means, or unknown]
File update date, if available: [label separately; do not substitute it]
Remaining time question: [what the source does not establish]

EVIDENCE
Source and locator: [URL/file name plus page, table, layer or passage]
Supplied statement: [what the source actually says]
Calculation or interpretation: [what you or the model added, or none]

UNRESOLVED
Unsupported conclusion: [what cannot yet be concluded]
Next check: [the specific evidence or clarification still needed]

Keep missing information visible as unknown; do not fill it with a guess.
Keep the source locator beside the statement for the next reader.

END BLANK CARD

FICTIONAL EXAMPLE — NO REAL SITE, DATASET OR ASSESSMENT

Scenario: Imagine a map response about a made-up building site. The only
supplied evidence is described as a city-level summary, with no observation
period given. No actual file or AI response has been examined for this example.

Question and intended use:
Can the city-level statement describe conditions at this particular site?
Use the card to identify what needs checking before interpreting the answer.

AREA
Question concerns: a made-up building site.
Evidence describes: an imagined city-level summary.
Match or unresolved difference: the scopes differ. The city statement alone
does not establish a site-level conclusion.

PERIOD
Relevant observation date or interval: unknown in this imagined scenario.
File update date: not supplied; it would be a separate label if available.
Remaining time question: when were the described conditions observed?

EVIDENCE
Source and locator: fictional label "City summary A"; no real URL or file.
Supplied statement: the summary describes the city, not this building site.
Calculation or interpretation: scope comparison only; the city statement
alone does not establish site conditions. No site measurement is calculated.

UNRESOLVED
Unsupported conclusion: any claim about the actual condition of the site.
Next check: find evidence with a stated observation period and relevant
geographic scope, then assess whether it supports the intended use. If those
questions remain unanswered, retain them as unresolved.

END FICTIONAL EXAMPLE

Educational material, not a property assessment or financial advice.
AI-assisted writing. No firsthand product test, company result, forecast or
investment recommendation is claimed.
